defaultPenalty: Up to ₹50 crore (residuary — Schedule to the DPDP Act, 2023)

provisions.title: Notice to the Data Principal before or at the time of collecting personal data
Notice must itemise what personal data is collected and the specified purpose of processing
Notice must be available in English or a language listed in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution
Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given by clear affirmative action
A request for consent must be accompanied by, or preceded by, the s.5 notice
A Data Principal may withdraw consent at any time, as easily as it was given
Certain legitimate uses do not require separate consent (e.g. voluntarily provided data, specified state functions)
General obligations of a Data Fiduciary: accuracy, processor contracts, and accountability for all processing done on its behalf
Reasonable security safeguards to prevent a personal data breach
Notify the Data Protection Board and every affected Data Principal in the event of a personal data breach
Erase personal data once the specified purpose is no longer served and retention is not required by law
Publish the business contact information of a Data Protection Officer or other person able to answer Data Principal questions about processing
Processing a child's personal data requires verifiable parental consent; no tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising directed at children
Additional obligations of a Significant Data Fiduciary (Data Protection Officer, independent auditor, Data Protection Impact Assessment)
Right to obtain a summary of personal data processed and the processing activities carried out
Right to correction, completion, updating and erasure of personal data
Right of grievance redressal against a Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager
Right to nominate another individual to exercise rights in the event of death or incapacity
Central Government may restrict transfer of personal data to certain countries; specified exemptions apply
